newsitem.title: INDIA: IMF chief starts talks with Indian leaders.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief starts talks with Indian leaders.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Michel Camdessus on Wednesday began a series of meetings with Indian officials to discuss the nation's economic problems and outlook.

Camdessus, on the last day of a four-day visit to India, said he would meet Finance Minister P. Chidambaram and other senior officials in the morning before having lunch with Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Asked about his agenda for the discussions, Camdessus told Reuters before entering the Finance Ministry: "The economic problems and perspectives of India. All of them."
The IMF head on Tuesday said he felt extremely positive about the government's budget for 1997/98 (April-March), which slashed taxes across the board and cut import tariffs.

He praised the government's decision to press ahead with market-oriented economic reforms launched in 1991 and said he was visiting India to see "the very remarkable impact" that the measures had had on the economy.

In 1991, India faced dwindling foreign exchange reserves and turned to the IMF for an emergency standby loan. It then began liberalising its economy, dismantling decades of socialist controls and inviting private and foreign investment.
Camdessus has stressed that he is visiting India to discuss the state of the economy and the future role of the IMF, and not to deal with an economic crisis.
The IMF chief arrived in New Delhi on Tuesday from the southwestern state of Goa, where he spent two days following his weekend arrival in the southern city of Madras.
He was set to leave for Hong Kong late on Wednesday after a news conference scheduled for 6 p.m. (1230 GMT).
